articleTitle: Temperature dependence of electrical parameters of coaxial cables
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: During long-term operation of safety cables, it is necessary to verify basic electrical parameters at a higher temperature than the temperature at which these parameters are tabulated by the manufacturer. Among cases when we need these dependencies belong accelerated thermal ageing carried out according to the Arrhenius approach, verification of the cable functionality during nuclear power plant (NPP) accident, etc. Due to requirements on monitoring of critical parameters in the process of ageing at elevated temperature, it is important to determine the effect of increased temperature on these parameters and its uncertainties. We also need these dependencies for correction of acceptance criteria of tests at elevated temperature (i.e. thermal ageing, radiation ageing at elevated temperature, simulation of accidental conditions). The same can be applied for diagnostic of the cable system in the industry, where the ambient temperature is increased. The aim of this paper is to compare and evaluate the temperature dependence of fundamental electrical parameters of cables, such as insulation resistance and frequency-dependent parameters (e.g. the capacity and dissipation factor). The experiment is conducted on three kinds of coaxial cable, each with a different kind of dielectric material: Teflon dielectric (PTFE), polyethylene (PE) and cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE).

articleTitle: Continuous condition monitoring of high voltage transformers by direct sensor monitoring of oil aging for a stable power network
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The new online oil sensor system, OilQSens®, enables continuous condition monitoring and power grid protection of high voltage transformers by sensor monitoring of oil aging. The requirements for transformers in the renewable energy rise. Ever more flexibility at a maximum operational reliability and a long life are required of them at the same time, so the requirements for the transformer oil grow correspondingly. The new online oil sensor system OilQSens® measures the components conductivity kappa, dielectric constant epsilon r and temperature T independently and calculates the breakdown-voltage, loss angle tan delta, acidification, and it looks promising to calculate also the humidity. The new approach utilizes sensor detection of chemical aging of the insulating oil and its inhibitors. Based on a very sensitive measurement method with high accuracy even small changes in the conductivity and dielectric constant of the transformer oil composition can be detected reliably. The new sensor system effectively controls the proper operation conditions of High Voltage Transformers, oil-filled circuit breakers and oil regeneration systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of dielectric properties of cable insulation by the extended voltage response method
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The voltage response method is based on the measurement of the decay and return voltages on a charged and shorted dielectric. From the initial slopes of these voltages, two material properties, namely the specific conductivity and the polarization conductivity can be determined. By changing the shorting time of the charged insulation the polarization processes can be examined separately and the whole polarization spectrum can be investigated more precisely. This paper introduces how the voltage response measurement technique is extended by the variation of discharging times. Measurements on oil-paper and polymeric insulated cables were carried out and the results have been compared. By this measurement method the differences of polarization processes of different insulating materials can be investigated more precisely.

articleTitle: Effect of dioctyl phthalate (DOP) plasticizing agent on the dielectric properties of PVC insulation
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The purpose of the paper is the investigation of the dielectric properties with respect to the plasticizer content in PVC materials. This polymer type is widely used as insulating and jacket material of cables in different areas of electric power engineering e.g. power plants. The dielectric relaxation of the synthetic plastics is a well-known phenomenon. During the measurement of insulation resistance, the development of steady state current requires quite long time due to the slow polarization processes in polymeric insulations. The investigation has been executed on thin film PVC samples with different plasticizer content and the dielectric processes have been measured by insulation resistance and voltage response measurement methods. By the usage of these parallel measurements, theory of slow polarization processes can be studied more precisely. In PVC the parallel methods lead to more exact results than if only one of measurements is used.

articleTitle: Diagnostic of induction motor using SFRA method
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Paper deals with experimental measurements and analysis of frequency responses SFRA (Sweep Frequency Response Analysis) measured on induction motors. For the induction motors will be established the measurement procedure of frequency responses. For the applying method SFRA for the purpose of diagnosis and analysis of the rotating machine state there are processed the results from the standard used electric diagnostic measurements for the rotating machines. The purpose of the experimental measurements is implementation of the SFRA method for the failure identification that arise in power Induction motors with the rated power over 10 kW.

articleTitle: Monitoring and diagnostic system of power plant electrical equipment
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Newly designed and developed monitoring and diagnostic system is determined for recording of analogue and binary signals coming from direct measurement and via common data communication standards. System is designed to be installed in distributed locations right next to power units electrical equipment which is being monitored. This system was developed in order to facilitate the initial commissioning of power units electrical equipment as well as to provide measurements and diagnostics during unit's normal operation and analyses of malfunction processes and transient conditions. The system fulfils all the requirements for the recording of needed signals within the tests and analyses of contemporary electrical equipment.

articleTitle: On the need for development of the highly stable source of digitally synthesized AC voltage with increased bandwidth for metrology and diagnostic applications
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Despite wide availability of AC voltage calibrators, digitally synthesized sources (DSS) in the form of function/arbitrary waveform generators (AWG) and radio-frequency (RF) generators there is still deficiency of AC voltage sources of sinusoidal voltage, able to synthesize signals from approximately 10 Hz up to hundreds of MHz with very high short-term stability of the amplitude and whose amplitude, in the order of a few volts, could be adjusted with high resolution, down to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> V/V or better. Adding the second channel could further increase the versatility and applications of the source. In this case the phase difference between sinusoidal voltages, generated by the source, should be adjustable with the resolution in the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−6</sup> radian. Such a source could be used in numerous metrology and diagnostic applications like primary standards of AC power and energy, voltage and current (AC-DC transfer systems), fully digital or digitally-assisted impedance bridges, insulation diagnostics systems and many others. Our paper will present a review and comparison of existing sources, results of their investigation, formulation of requirements and preliminary proposals of the design of the new source.

articleTitle: Noise measurement of power transformer
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Noise is a very important parameter of power transformer. The noise is represented by measured sound power. For sound power determination of the power transformer there are methods standardized by EN 60076-10. These standard methods are based on measurement of sound pressure or sound intensity in few points only. The information about dissipated sound power is not enough in some cases. Due to there was designed method for localization of most noisy parts of the transformer. The method is based on sound intensity mapping in a regular grid. Obtained data are used for creation colour map of sound intensity and sound power calculation.

articleTitle: Monitoring and diagnosis of electrical equipment using a web software. Health index and remaining lifetime estimation
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Electrical equipment monitoring and diagnosis are very important for both users and manufacturers. In order to assess equipment conditions, certain periodical tests and measurements must be made and monitoring and diagnosis systems must be installed, together with special software. This paper presents a web software (DiagConsole), which can be accessed remotely using a web browser. The software gathers online and off-line data, estimating the equipment's health index, remaining lifetime and presenting the type of maintenance needed to prolong it. A condition assessment report is automatically built and can very well replace the traditional paper database. The web software is installed in two key power plants in Romania. Several electrical equipment are monitored and diagnosed (power transformers, hydrogenerators, etc.) and two power transformers and one hydrogenerator are presented as condition assessment examples.

articleTitle: Possibilities of modification of polymer/SiO2 composite by various types of carrier
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The main aim of this paper is to describe possibilities of modification of polymer insulating materials by various types of carrier. The major problem of currently used insulation system is their inhomogeneous structure. Therefore, there is an efforts to develop material that is macroscopically homogeneous. New composite materials are created using nano-particles silica (~1 wt %) and epoxy type of resin. Polyethylene terephthalate (PET), polyethylene naphthalate (PEN) and fabric with micrometric thicknesses were chosen as carrier for this research. Composites were created by using a mixing method, in which a nano-fillers were applied to the epoxy resin and applied on PET, PEN or glass fabric carrier component. The dissipation factor, volume resistivity, dielectric strength and polarization indexes were measured to determine the electrical insulating properties.

articleTitle: Reaction mechanism of transformer oil pyrolysis based on TG-DSC and molecular simulation
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Thermal fault threatens the safe and stable operation of oil filled equipment. Based on TG-DSC and ReaxFF (reactive force field), in this paper, the reaction of molecular dynamics simulation method was used to establish the simulation model of mineral insulating oil molecules under different temperatures and to study dynamic pyrolysis process and produce regularity of gaseous molecules in transformer oil. First, thermal analysis technique TG-DSC is used to observe the quality and energy changes during the process of transformer oil decomposition. Then, by using reactive reaction force field, the three typical hydrocarbons in transformer oil-alkane, cycloalkane and aromatic is simulated in a liquid system and the microscopic decomposition mechanism of transformer oil is studied. Through the establishment of a liquid system consisting of three different kinds of hydrocarbons, and the minimization of energy balance system, the pyrolysis of them in NVT system is simulated under different temperatures. The initial decomposition temperatures of the three kinds of hydrocarbons is that alkane is lower than cycloalkane and aromatic is the highest. Then the relationship between temperature and the process of pyrolysis is concluded. This study reveals the pyrolysis dynamic mechanism of the transformer oil on the atomic level, corresponding to the real pyrolysis successfully.

articleTitle: Analysis of short-circuit effects on transformer state by frequency method
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Article presents analysis of insulating and mechanical state of transformers considering possible effect of short-circuit currents on the winding. The first part of the article is focused to negative activity thermal and mechanical effects of short-circuit currents. The last part of the article is focused to the simulation method which shows the mechanical stress caused by the short circuit-currents. Finally, the article presents experimental frequency methods of diagnostics for analysis of the short-circuit effects on insulating and mechanical transformer state.

articleTitle: New complex nanocomposite DGEBA
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper deals with complex nanocomposite, which was developed. The nanocomposite is based on epoxy resin modified by nanosilica and nanofabric. As a matrix was used epoxy resin DGEBA based on bisphenol A with hardener Laromin C260 and particles hydrophobic nanosilica - AEROSIL R 974. As filler Ultramid - Polyamide 6 garneted in an electrostatic field. It was verified optimum amount Nano additives into the matrix 1% hm. and adjustment of flowability of resin by incorporating thinner Phenyl glycidyl ether - FGE. The final composite has a very good electrical properties. Extremely good absorption current (minute polarization index 3.59, the volume resistivity of the order of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">16</sup>), very good dielectric strength 38.38 kV / mm and excellent dielectric loss tan δ = 4.7 E-03. Its properties exceeds the standard today the use of insulating systems and is very good new promising insulating material. Because it contains components both the matrix and binder we can speak of a complex nanocomposite.

articleTitle: Developments in UHF PD monitoring system for switchgear and transformer paper title
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: It is important to obtain the operational safety of the Switchgear, Transformer because The electrical facility plays a great role in ensuring the reliability of power supply. For that reason, many researchers develop various methods to diagnose their condition. In this paper, it is presented that online Partial Discharge (PD) detection system of condition monitoring for MCSG (7.2kV, 22.9kV), Dry type Transformer based on ultra-high frequency (UHF) measurements. In order to detect PD Signal, UHF Sensor and Data Acquisition Unit (DAU), HMI (PD monitoring S/W) were developed. Four artificial insulation defect models were designed to generate UHF PD signals and PD Signal was detected by a UHF Sensor. This work could contribute to develop Advanced Diagnosis & preventive system.

articleTitle: Modelling of dielectric processes in oil-paper insulation for replacement of Return Voltage Measurement
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In Hungary, the main diagnostic method for power transformers has been the Return Voltage Measurement (RVM) for decades, however, the measurement time is quite long. In order to get information about the condition (moistening, ageing) of the oil-paper insulation, the changes of the RVM curves have to be compared. In this study, the authors introduce a method, wherewith the faster voltage response (VR) measurement can provide the curves of the RVM, with acceptable error. The newly developed method bases on an iteration method that describes an equivalent circuit of the transformer insulation containing only five Debye elements. The method has been tested on a transformer insulation model and also on a model insulation R-C circuit. The results show, from the results of VR measurement the elements of the equivalent circuit can be determined and the Return Voltage Measurement can be simulated in an appropriate software.

articleTitle: Natural ester — Moisture and acidity issue
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Electrical insulating system is an important part of the electrical equipment. In the case of high voltage transformers, their electrical insulating system is composed of insulating oil and paper, the quality of used insulating fluid is a decisive factor for the service life and reliability of the transformer. The transformer oil is also a carrier of information of the state of the transformer because the degradation influences (temperature, solid contaminants, etc.) are during operation causing aging of the insulating oil. The aging of transformer oil leads to deterioration of the quality of oil that the oil must be replaced with new or regenerated oil. Given the current emphasis on environmental protection and economical operation, it is recommended the refining of oil before its replacement with a new one. This article deals with the refining of natural rapeseed oil through the adsorbent. The refining of rapeseed oil removes acidic substances and improves the acid number and its properties.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic power plants contribution to the flicker level in the medium voltage energy network. Case study
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In recent years, renewable energy sources, particularly photovoltaic power plants, have become important sources of energy for the National Energy System in Romania. Connecting them to the energy grid may cause frequency variations or fast voltage variations (flicker), significant problems in terms of power quality. The severity of these problems depends directly on the percentage of the photovoltaic system integration, geographic location and grid typology. In Romania, photovoltaic power plants that are connected to the medium voltage networks must comply with legislation (NT. 30, Ord. 74, Ord. 59, NT E 012, EN 50160). Given these aspects, this paper aims to conduct a study on the contribution of photovoltaic power plants regarding the flicker level in the medium voltage network; in this particular case, a 5 MW PV plant is presented.

articleTitle: Analysis on quality of diagnostic processes in power electrical engineering using combined methods of lead six sigma and fuzzy approaches
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Process control is a statistics and engineering discipline that deals with architectures, mechanisms and algorithms. In power electrical engineering and diagnostics field it is important to evaluate which are the critical factors influencing on the quality of the process, as well as to determine which the factors are leading to the failures. Applying Lean Six Sigma methodologies on different stages can help to benefit on many process levels: to evaluate the efficiency of the chosen diagnostic schema, make the diagnostic process run faster and more stable with less failures and can help to create a systematic approach in all the mentioned benefits above. In turn Fuzzy approach and Fuzzy logic based systems with their capability to deal with incomplete information, imprecision, and incorporation of qualitative knowledge shows a great potential for application in electric system fault detection as well as serve as a good basis for measuring effectiveness of chosen methods. Combining different type of quality methods and fuzzy mathematical tools will provide a broader view on the performed process and will help to create an understanding where it can be improved, and thus control and improve the quality. Fault tolerance design has been examined by Lean Six Sigma approach, as well as identification of the fault itself has been analyzed using fuzzy expert system.

articleTitle: Nonlinear distortion of C/V characteristic — Useful tool for diagnostics of electrically conductive adhesives: Theoretical background, measuring equipment, selected applications
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Electrically conductive adhesives are used in electrical engineering to substitute lead free solders for conductive joining of components with low resistivity against heat, for mounting of integrated circuits with fine-pitch and ultra-fine-pitch packages, and for adhesive assembly on flex printed circuit boards. Conductive adhesives are materials composed of insulating matrix and conductive filler, usually silver flakes for adhesives with isotropic electrical conductivity are used. A conductive network whose resistance depends mainly on the resistance between the individual particles of the filler is formed inside the conductive adhesive. The main component of the resistance between the particles is a tunnel resistance. The basic theory of formation of tunnel resistance and the generation of the third harmonic component on such resistance when the tunnel junction is powered by a sinusoidal voltage is described in the article. Two basic principles of measuring of third harmonics, which represents nonlinearity and using of this diagnostics for study of changes in adhesive joints caused by mechanical and climatic ageing are also described.

articleTitle: High frequency high voltage probe embedded into an extremely low inductivity high voltage supply connection
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: For some high voltage devices the frequency response is of interest. Besides the generation of high voltage high frequency signals, the transmission and measurement of the signal is a challenge. Due to the great physical dimensions of high voltage assemblies, the inductance of these is very high, which limits the frequencies that can be used to test. It is critical to know the input signal. The more information about the input signal is known, the better the response can be calculated. The impact of high voltage dividers cannot be neglected at higher frequencies (kHz and up). Therefore a different reference is of need. To solve these problems, a high voltage connector with extremely low inductance and an integrated voltage probe has been developed. By reducing the inductivity of the connection, the frequency range of the test signal can be increased. The integrated voltage probe makes it possible to precisely measure the input signal, serving as reference. Therefore it is possible to precisely calculate the frequency response of the DUT, possibly leading to better diagnostics.

articleTitle: Porous tapes for VPI insulation systems of high voltage stator windings of large rotating electrical machines based on the mica paper with a large surface weight
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Cogebi, member of ELCIM Group, is a traditional producer of mica insulation materials. Especially porous mica insulation tapes are important components of HV insulation systems of largest turbine generators. Continuous innovation process of glass backed VPI tapes is targeted on an operational voltage gradient increase of the stator insulation. Higher content of mica in the main wall insulation can be a solution of the goal.

articleTitle: Study of die attachment on DBC substrate
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper describes the results of investigations concerning the behaviour and joint quality of various die attachment materials on DBC (Direct Bonded Copper) Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> based substrates. A comparative study of influence of various material on joint quality was realized. Experimental samples were reflowed in a vacuum reflow oven, and in a vapour phase soldering (VPS) chamber. For the first time were applied new developed solder materials (Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">96.5</sub>Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3.5</sub> and Sn<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">95.9</sub>Cu<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>Ag<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.1</sub> alloys) in the form of thin ribbons. The new metals and alloys were prepared by the rapid solidification technique - melt spinning at a cooling rate of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> °C/s. First measurements show that the new materials meet high requirements on joints properties: better thermal conductivity and mechanical strengths, less voids and better thermo-mechanical reliability. The thin ribbons based on the melt spinning (rapidly cooled) materials are a promising candidate for use in the die attachment in power electronics.

articleTitle: Insulation evaluation of capacitive equipment by power loss density
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper presents a new approach to assess the insulation condition of capacitive equipment based on power loss density. Power loss angle is an important parameter to evaluate the insulation condition of capacitive equipment, but it cannot represent the actual power loss of the equipment without considering its capacitance and volume. In the paper, through listing some engineering cases and theoretical analysis, the power loss of the capacitive equipment is calculated under different applied voltage and converted to the corresponding power loss density per unit volume which normalize the operation voltage, capacitance and volume of the equipment. By analyzing the power loss density, insulation evaluation of different kinds of capacitive equipment is identified. Based on the power loss density, qualitative diagnosis and assessment for the capacitive equipment have been presented, which will be supportive for condition assessment and diagnosis of capacitive equipment.

articleTitle: Complex dielectric constant of various insulating fluids
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Maintenance and condition monitoring of high voltage transformers is of utmost importance, so that local defects can be eliminated before they grow to a failure. The most important part of a transformer with respect to reliability is its oil-paper insulation. Local defects formed here can be detected and located by the means of UHF partial discharge measurement. The applicability of the method relies heavily on the signals to propagate to the sensors through the oil. To determine the properties of the propagation, the high frequency behaviour of the oil must be understood. This article presents the results of a series of measurements on various types of insulating fluids. The applied method relies on the measurement of the impedance of the oil at high frequency. With this, the complex frequency dependent dielectric constant of the oil can be determined. This later enables the calculation to determine whether the PD signals can be detected at the sensors.

articleTitle: Diagnostic system for off-line diagnosis of MV cables
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Actual condition and the remaining lifetime of medium voltage cables are of high interest for a condition based asset management. By the conduction of an artificial aging experiment on paper insulated lead covered cables, the aging behavior of this cable type could be pointed out. With this knowledge, a new project with the focus on application in field has been started. Within the project, a diagnostic system for off-line diagnosis of medium voltage cables has been developed. After a short description of the aging experiment and its results, the measurement system and some results from the field measurements will be presented.

articleTitle: Simulation model of flashover process on insulator string exposed to the impulse voltages
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The paper deals with a mathematical simulation model for the prediction of flashover voltages of suspension insulator string during the high voltage impulse voltage tests, when various shapes of impulse voltages are applied. The physical background of the streamer-leader flashover process with assumptions and constrains needed for mathematical simulations is described. The approximation of electric field distribution during the flashover process is carried out by finite element method calculation. After that, the final computer algorithm is proposed and verified on real experimental measurements in the high voltage laboratory. The realized computer program allows to calculate the flashover voltage for various shapes of impulse voltages and moreover, to take into consideration an influence of pollution layer on insulator surface. Presented comparison with experimental measurement confirms that the proposed simulation model can give reasonable accurate values of flashover voltages which are sufficient for test engineers.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of fluid systems with dispersed nanoparticles
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Natural oils are divided into vegetable and mineral oils. Compared with vegetable oils, the mineral oils show better dielectric properties, however, they are dangerous for the living environment and their flammability is higher. Recently, additives in the form of dispersed nanoparticles, especially SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, ZnO, Al<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, are used in the effort to improve certain dielectric properties of mineral oils. This paper is mainly focused on the summary of dielectric properties of mineral oils with dispersed nanoparticles. Next research will be focused on the dielectric properties of vegetable oils with dispersed nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Medium voltage equipment diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Due to the high amount of installed devices in the Hungarian medium voltage grid it is important to be aware of the exact root causes of malfunctions. If the root causes are known it is possible to prevent the undesired malfunctions, therefore the operational safety can be increased. There are continuous investigations performed in the High Voltage Laboratory of Budapest Institute of Technology and Economics to find out the root causes of malfunctions, which were previously categorized as “unknown” by distribution system operators. The research involves the study of malfunction descriptive databases, the environmental effects (lightning databases) and the examination of malfunctioned devices. The main aim is to reproduce the malfunctions under laboratory circumstances to verify the results and to develop new laboratory tests in order to reveal the weaknesses of individual devices; this paper focuses on the analysis of medium voltage metal-oxide surge arresters (MOA).

articleTitle: Detection of faults in rotor-windings of turbogenerators
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper should give an overview of different measurement methods for detecting faults in rotor-windings of turbogenerators and explains their principal functionality in detail. Advantages and disadvantages of each individual measurement are summarized and compared. In addition theoretical calculation models to evaluate the specific methods are illustrated while at the same time the accuracy of this theoretical models are validated with the help of practical testing.

articleTitle: Permittivity determination of composite materials based on a 3D electric field model
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Composite materials are an integral part of electrical systems; however, the determination of their dielectric properties through calculation is sometimes problematic. The aim of this paper is to demonstrate a way to determine the effective permittivity of a composite material by using a 3D electric field model while exploiting the distribution of electric energy and to verify the results by values obtained experimentally. Two types of samples were investigated: with the inclusion phase evenly distributed across the host phase in one plane and in two planes. The experiment was conducted by means of Tettex 2830/2831, a precise dielectric analyzer for solid and liquid dielectrics and Tettex 2914, a special temperature-controlled electrode system. The computation was performed by COMSOL Multiphysics professional software. The results obtained through a 3D model corresponded to the results of the experiment.

articleTitle: Laboratory measurement results of a spatially-resolved diagnostic method for power cables using travelling waves
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In this paper, laboratory measurement results of a spatially-resolved diagnostic method for power cables will be presented. This new method uses travelling waves and their interference characteristics to generate local energy losses inside the test object. This losses can be measured and give a qualitative indication of the local physical condition of the cable insulation. The method has been tested in several simulations, which are based on discretized cable models, which were sectionally degraded. Also different lengths and different types of cables have been tested. From this set of laboratory measurements, the most significant results will be presented in this paper. In the described measurement results, the proposed approach of a diagnostic method shows local degradations of power cables and coaxial signal cables both in simulation and laboratory measurements, which cannot be detected by established reflectometry methods.

articleTitle: Fractal simulation of breakdown in oil impregnated paper at pulsating DC voltage
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The oil impregnated paper is one of the typical composite structure containing a large number of cavities, which are filled with insulating oil through oil impregnation. In this paper, the oil-impregnated paper structure is simplified and an electrical breakdown model is developed to describe the breakdown progress in oil impregnated paper at pulsating DC voltage. Based on the traditional WZ model, the space discharge and physical time are introduced in the proposed model. The influence of temperature is also investigated. The skeleton types of discharge structure, discharge velocity, and charge movement during the breakdown are simulated. The breakdown simulation results show that the conductivity variation of insulation paper is an important factor which reduces the breakdown voltage under pulsating DC voltage at high temperature.

articleTitle: A special risk during live-line maintenance
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The main purpose of arc protection is the prevention of the initiation of an electric arc, and to decrease the emitted energy of the arc to the lowest possible level. If the hazard is not negligible, personal protective equipment must be used. In case of live-line maintenance (LLM) in high voltage (HV) systems, the use of personal protective equipment against arc is not common, but the chance of the development of an electric arc has to be evaluated in this case, too. During live work in HV systems, the possible appearance of an electric arc means extreme danger; due to the high power, the magnitude of the current of the arc may reach the range of several kiloampers. For this reason, the live-line personnel in the vicinity of the arc suffers extremely high levels of different kind of harmful loads. The main aim of this article is to investigate the possibility of the initialization of an electric arc during HV LLM and to analyze the proper ways of handling this kind of risk.

articleTitle: Testing of high voltage cable lines by damped ac technique — A case study
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: In this paper, a case-study is presented, which emphasizes the role of local degradation detection besides the general condition assessment of the high voltage cable line insulation. The applied damped AC method provides several diagnostic parameters e.g. PD inception and extinction voltages, PD map and loss factor therefore it is an effective tool in cable diagnosis. The partial discharge tests detected the weak points of the investigated cable line, which were mounted with porcelain terminations. After the replacement of the terminations the cable line has become PD free. This case study emphasizes that from the point of view of reliability, the weakest points of the HV cable lines are the cable accessories. The time of the failure of these components cannot be predicted exactly, the only way to prevent the failure is the regular diagnostic testing of critical cable lines.

articleTitle: Ageing of used composite insulation systems under different voltage stress
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: This paper describes the assessing the lifetime curves of composite insulation under different kind of voltage stress. This covers several areas that are important for using the electrical insulation properly. First one is the composite insulation. The use of this kind of insulation is rising, new types of composites are being invented and investigated with the aim for the best achievable properties. These insulation structures are inhomogeneous that causes problems with PD etc. This kind of insulation has its use in high voltage applications as is large rotating machines (e.g. turbo and hydro generators). This composite was aged by a different kind of voltage applied. First, the AC voltage was applied, as it is the most commonly used voltage. The composite was also subjected to the DC voltage, as it is rising, thanks to the usage of power electronics in DC drives, which generates voltage spikes. This brings new problems that shorten the lifetime of the electrical machines.

articleTitle: Determining the influence of the air gap during the inspection of the rotor insulation of a synchronous machine in operation
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: The aim of this article is to determine the impact of variability of the air gap above the individual poles of the rotor of the synchronous machine. The main is focused on the calculation of the effect of the air gap in the diagnosis interturn short circuits. There is a simulated course of the induction in the air gap for the rotor with a perfect roundness and for the real rotor. Subsequently, the induced voltage on the measuring coil is calculated. In conclusion the waveforms are compared and the influence of the air gap is defined to measure the interturn short circuits.

articleTitle: The evaluation of the condition of high-voltage system with using accelerated voltage time tests and design of main wall insulation thickness for stator bar of generator stator winding

abstract: Assessment of the optimal thickness for mainwall insulation tube in the slot part of the stator bar belongs to an important item in the design of the insulation system from view of the functionality and operational reliability of the rotating machines.

articleTitle: Usage of sampling inspection as a tool for quality assurance
publicationTitle: 2016 Conference on Diagnostics in Electrical Engineering (Diagnostika)
abstract: Competitive pressure is forcing suppliers, manufacturers and customers to increase constantly requirements on the quality of products or services. For this reason all levels of quality management tools are used. Using seven basic tools for quality assurance is obvious; moreover seven new tools were defined from this reason. The application of statistical tools is growing, too, mostly depending on the needs and demands for accuracy and product quantity, especially statistical process control and sampling inspection. The summary of standards recommending various kinds of sampling inspections shows that the orientation in the area is not as easy as it should be, e.g. a decision tree is absent, border conditions are not so clearly defined etc. This gap will be covered by this contribution. The full paper will deal with the analysis of 29 standards, which can be applied in the Czech industry.
